title: Activists mull constitutional case against police arrest at MV Barima vigil
summary: Civil society activists who were arrested during a government-organised vigil for MV Barima victims are weighing a constitutional case against the State. The group, including Sherlina Nageer, was detained on Wednesday night while picketing peacefully at Kingston Seawall with signs demanding the resignation and prosecution of Public Works Minister Juan Edghill. No charges were laid and a senior police officer offered what the activists called an insincere, conditional apology, which Nageer rejected as disproportionate to the assault and rights violation. The women intend to seek legal advice before approaching the High Court under Article 147 of the Constitution, and to complain to the Guyana Police Force's Office of Professional Responsibility.

The aim of any case is to establish that police cannot arbitrarily arrest peaceful demonstrators or remove them from scenes of lawful assembly.

The assault and rights violation are like real, actual serious things and saying you're 'sorry and just get out of my office', to me the scale is not balanced. — Sherlina Nageer, civil society activist detained at the vigil

title: Police detain, then apologise to, peaceful protesters at national vigil for MV Barima victims
summary: The Guyana Police Force is under criticism after officers arrested and briefly detained three female activists — Sherlina Nageer, Salima Bacchus-Hinds and Romola Lucas — during the government-organised national prayer service at Kingston Seawall on 22 July. Five women had stood on the periphery of the Bandstand with signs demanding accountability for what they called a completely preventable tragedy; police moved in about an hour into the event after the group relocated near the 'One Guyana' sign, citing unlawful protest, absence of a permit and illegal signs. All three were released on their own recognisance after roughly an hour, and the activists say police dropped all charges and apologised at a meeting with the Police Commander on Thursday morning. The women still condemned the episode as State overreach under Article 147 of the Constitution and filed a complaint with the Office of Professional Responsibility, while demanding an independent investigation, an overhaul of hinterland and coastal transport, and Edghill's immediate resignation.

title: 3rd person detained as police probe continues in MV Barima tragedy
summary: A superintendent of the Transport and Harbours Department has become the third person arrested in the police investigation into the MV Barima capsizing. The officer oversaw Georgetown port operations, including ferry loading and ticket sales, and Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said he was invited for questioning at the Criminal Investigations Department, arrived with legal counsel and was then detained. The ferry's captain and a crew member remain in custody after blood tests detected marijuana in their systems. The vessel left Georgetown around 15:00h on Saturday with 179 persons for Port Kaituma, met rough seas near the Pomeroon River mouth, listed and capsized, with a distress signal around 23:01h triggering a GDF, MARAD and civilian vessel response; authorities also found manifest discrepancies and an investigation commission is being established.

title: STATE ASSUMED RISK FOR UNINSURED MV BARIMA — EDGHILL
summary: Public Works Minister Juan Edghill confirmed on Tuesday that the state-owned MV Barima carried no commercial insurance when it capsized, and that the Government of Guyana therefore carried the financial risk itself. Edghill said it has long been the practice for state-owned vessels to operate without commercial insurance, with the government assuming responsibility for losses and any compensation, meaning replacement costs, lost government cargo and compensation could fall on the state and ultimately taxpayers. Officials did not say whether a dedicated fund or formal self-insurance mechanism exists for maritime accidents, and what compensation may be available to survivors and bereaved families remains unclear. At the same briefing Prime Minister Mark Phillips called the manifest failure 'a breakdown in the system' to be examined by the Commission of Inquiry, and the government said 53 bodies had been recovered and 76 survivors verified as of 6 p.m. Tuesday.

title: APNU demands compensation for families of MV Barima tragedy
summary: At its weekly press conference on Friday, APNU demanded fair and adequate compensation for survivors and the families of those who died in the 18 July MV Barima capsizing, and called for the removal of Public Works Minister Juan Edghill and Public Utilities and Aviation Minister Deodat Indar pending an independent probe. MP Saiku Andrews, who shadows the public works ministry, said funeral assistance should be no less than $1M per victim, noting that some families have been offered a mere $300,000, which would not even cover the burial. APNU said it has assembled a legal team, that 15 attorneys have so far expressed willingness to represent families, and that lawyers have raised concern at the Guyana Bar Association's silence on legal aid, with the Mahdia dorms fire cited as a precedent where families signed off on compensation packages without independent legal advice. The party also called for a comprehensive safety review of all ferries operating in Guyana, with Andrews describing the disaster as a systemic failure.

title: Guyana to await inquiry before deciding on compensation for MV Barima tragedy
summary: The Guyana government will keep covering funeral and burial expenses and immediate assistance for families of the MV Barima dead, but will decide on compensation only after an independent Commission of Inquiry reports. Prime Minister Brigadier (Ret'd) Mark Phillips told a news conference on Wednesday that the focus is on recovering bodies and financing burial and funeral rites, and stressed that current financial assistance is not deemed compensation but the government's responsibility in times like this. He said the government intends to mount the Commission of Inquiry as early as possible once the rescue and recovery operation closes, and that the commission's report and recommendations will guide whether compensation is warranted and how it is handled. Search and recovery continues with 19 vessels and three aircraft deployed, smaller GDF, Coast Guard and MARAD vessels searching inland waterways, and technical teams assessing the wreck for recovery.

title: APNU submits parliamentary motion to discuss scope of MV Barima inquiry
summary: APNU Lead MP Dr. Terrence Campbell wrote to Speaker of the National Assembly Manzoor Nadir on Friday, ahead of Monday's Sitting, asking for an adjournment of the Assembly to debate the Terms of Reference for a Commission of Inquiry into the MV Barima sinking. He qualified the request as urgent and of public importance, citing substantial property damage, significant loss of life and acute public concern, and pointed to concerns over vessel seaworthiness, regulatory compliance, oversight by maritime authorities, the search and rescue response, availability of other vessels and prevention of recurrence. APNU described the 18 July disaster as the worst maritime disaster in Guyana's recent history with a death toll already surpassing 70, and stated the immediate need for a fully independent CoI with clear terms of reference. The party tabled a proposed ToR with eight areas of focus and asked the Assembly also to settle timeframe, membership criteria and budgetary arrangements.
key_facts: Dr. Terrence Campbell, APNU Lead MP, submitted correspondence to Speaker Manzoor Nadir on Friday ahead of Monday's Sitting.

Almost 200 passengers and crew members were aboard, along with over 200 tonnes of cargo; the vessel was heading to Port Kaituma, Region One.

Concerns cited: seaworthiness of vessels, regulatory compliance, oversight by maritime authorities, search and rescue response, availability of other vessels, measures to prevent recurrence.

Proposed ToR identifies eight key areas: establishing facts; determining cause and contributing factors; examining search-and-rescue response adequacy; assessing regulatory framework and oversight practices; examining allegations of negligence or misconduct; recommending safety improvements; requiring documents and witnesses; adopting interim protective measures.
Campbell also asked the Assembly to discuss timeframe, membership criteria including independence and expertise, and budgetary arrangements for the commission.

title: Guyana Government tightens ferry safety procedures following MV Barima tragedy
summary: CMC wire report carried by the Jamaica Observer on the state of the MV Barima recovery operation and the government's response one week after the sinking. President Irfaan Ali, briefing families at the Charity Operations Centre, said specialist divers had completed two dives with a third planned and had recovered one more body from the wreck, bringing the toll to 72. Prime Minister Mark Phillips said the government is strengthening compliance with standard operating procedures across the ferry service, including stricter adherence to ticketing and passenger management, after it was confirmed people boarded without being ticketed; CCTV from the departure stelling established 179 people were aboard. The opposition APNU pressed the Speaker to have the National Assembly set terms of reference for a commission of inquiry, with the PNCR warning of mass protests, and cited a March 2026 rehabilitation tender showing engineers had flagged hull deterioration months before the disaster.
key_facts: One additional body recovered from the wreck on Friday 24 July; death toll rose to 72.
Official manifest listed 116 passengers and a 17-member crew; authorities said as many as 179 passengers and crew may have been aboard; 76 survived.

PM Phillips: government strengthening compliance with standard operating procedures across the ferry service.

An independent Commission of Inquiry is being established and will investigate how manifest-versus-actual passenger discrepancies were allowed to occur at the Transport and Harbours Department.
APNU wrote to Speaker Manzoor Nadir via parliamentary leader Dr Terrence Campbell proposing the Assembly meet the following Monday to consider establishing the commission.

APNU terms of reference sought: timeline, passenger and manifest records, cargo, weather and navigation conditions; vessel maintenance and seaworthiness; crew qualifications and training; compliance with national maritime laws, licences and safety standards; adequacy and timeliness of search-and-rescue response; regulatory framework, oversight, inspection regimes and enforcement practices; allegations of negligence, misconduct, corruption or breach of statutory duties; production of documents and summoning of witnesses; a full public report within a specified timeframe.

APNU's Saiku Andrews said the March 2026 docking and rehabilitation tender's Bills of Quantities required examination of approximately 10,000 square metres of hull plating and frames, with deteriorated sections renewed where necessary.
APNU's Dexter Todd said 15 lawyers had been assembled to protect survivors' interests, and that the captain and two crew members remained in police custody.
notable_quotes: They are making progress in cutting things open and clearing, and as a result, they have been able to recover one more body so far from the wreck — Irfaan Ali, President of Guyana

We intend to ensure that we bring the necessary pressure to bear so that this matter can be dealt with with much dispatch and by that, I mean, if it means that we have to organise mass political activities — Sherwin Benjamin, General Secretary of the People's National Congress Reform (PNCR)

The real issue is that the Government's own engineers identified the need to examine the hull, replace deteriorated steel, replace wasted hatch beams, replace zinc anodes, service critical components and carry out ultrasonic thickness testing only months before the tragedy — Saiku Andrews, APNU parliamentarian

title: Indigenous Leaders Honor Victims Of M.V Barima Tragedy At National Toshao's Council Conference
summary: The 2026 National Toshaos Council Conference closed on Friday 24 July at the Arthur Chung Conference Centre with Indigenous leaders pausing deliberations to pray for and pay tribute to victims of the MV Barima disaster. The week-long gathering had itself been delayed by the capsizing of the 87-year-old state-operated ferry off the Essequibo Coast, and brought village leaders, ministers and parliamentarians together in solidarity with affected hinterland communities. Amerindian Affairs Minister Sarah Browne-Shadeek, in her inaugural address to the conference, offered condolences and said she hoped multi-agency investigations would deliver full clarity. Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed told the assembly not to let anyone silence their voices, while village leaders pressed for long-term economic assistance, educational aid for affected children and sustained relief for orphans and bereaved families.

title: National Toshaos Council Conference Postponed To A Day Later Amid Mv Barima Tragedy – Location Of M.V Barima Conformed
summary: The ceremonial opening of the 2026 National Toshaos Council Conference at the Arthur Chung Conference Centre, Liliendaal, was postponed by a day as hundreds of Amerindian leaders and village captains gathered in grief over the MV Barima sinking. Vice President Bharrat Jagdeo, addressing an impromptu open consultation session on Monday afternoon, confirmed 10 bodies had officially been recovered and that search-and-rescue divers had pinpointed the exact underwater coordinates of the submerged vessel. The government outlined immediate measures: an emergency hotline for families to report missing relatives, cross-referencing of public submissions against hospital admission logs and field rescue manifests, presidential site visits by Irfaan Ali across Region One and Region Two, and continued police custody for crew members who tested positive for cannabis traces. Organisers set the formal opening for Tuesday, July 21, 2026, under the theme of empowering leadership and sustainable village economies, with President Ali to give the feature address covering hinterland infrastructure and river transport safety.

title: Govt introduces interim cargo service to ensure essential supplies reach Port Kaituma
summary: The Ministry of Public Works announced an interim cargo arrangement to keep essential supplies flowing to Port Kaituma while normal transport services remain disrupted after the MV Barima sinking. An open barge will carry cargo and essential supplies only to the Region One community, with no passengers accommodated. Loading begins Saturday, July 25 at the Kingston Goods Wharf, with departure from Georgetown set for Monday, July 27 at 5:00 p.m., and the ministry warned that weather-sensitive items must be securely packaged because the open barge exposes cargo to the elements. The service is free of charge and is intended to sustain critical supplies until regular shipping operations resume.

title: Nine victims of MV Barima tragedy laid to rest
summary: Kaieteur News reports that nine MV Barima victims were buried on Thursday 23 July in their respective communities, with cabinet members and regional officials attending the services. The paper recaps the voyage: the ferry left the Transport and Harbours Department wharf at Kingston, Georgetown at about 3:15 p.m. on Saturday July 18 bound for Port Kaituma, and the 87-year-old vessel sank roughly seven miles offshore near Iron Punt in the vicinity of the Pomeroon River. Government figures suggest at least 179 people were aboard; 72 had died, 65 of them positively identified by families, and 76 were rescued. The report names the nine buried and details the international search effort involving the Trinidad and Tobago Coast Guard and Brazilian Navy, 19 vessels and three aircraft, and three days of national mourning declared by President Ali.

title: New Amsterdam waives burial plot fees for families of MV Barima victims
summary: The Mayor and Town Council of New Amsterdam announced that families of MV Barima victims will not pay for burial plots at the Stanleytown Cemetery, and that anyone who had already paid before Wednesday's decision will be fully refunded through the council's treasurer's office. Mayor Wainwright McIntosh, accompanied by Councillor Pollyanne Schultz, visited the homes of families of the confirmed dead and of the still missing on Wednesday 22 July, including the family of 28-year-old Kevin Wilson, whose death was confirmed Monday evening. Other visits went to the family of 56-year-old sailor Raymond Somra of Islington, East Bank Berbice, still unaccounted for after more than four decades at sea; to Paul Seepersaud, 44, of Vryman's Erven, whose body was recovered Tuesday; and to Devon Mars of Sandvoort Village, whose identity was yet to be confirmed. The municipality also hosted a candlelight vigil and a night of prayer, as the government observed three days of national mourning.

title: Guyana ferry disaster: families demand answers as around 100 feared dead
summary: Al Jazeera, with AP, reports the expected death toll from Guyana's worst maritime disaster in decades climbing to around 100, with 76 of roughly 179 people aboard surviving and 53 bodies recovered as of Tuesday. Families gathered at Charity awaiting news, among them Samantha Ramin, who lost two of her three children and whose baby boy was still missing. Passengers and survivors allege the 87-year-old MV Barima was dangerously overloaded with people and heavy cargo including engines, vehicles, fuel containers and commercial goods, that engine trouble shortly after departure was repaired at sea rather than prompting a return, and that crew dismissed water ingress as routine; the government maintains the ferry was under its passenger and cargo capacity limits. Prime Minister Mark Phillips said the government has nothing to hide and pledged legal consequences for anyone responsible, while police detained the rescued captain and at least one other crew member, both reportedly testing positive for marijuana, and officials said a US$12.7 million Indian-built replacement ferry was awaiting completion of a special pier at Port Kaituma.

Government officials say the ferry was under its capacity limits for both passengers and cargo but say conflicting accounts make firm conclusions premature.
The head of the Maritime Administration Department said a full investigation is needed to establish how the vessel was loaded and whether supervisory staff acted properly.
PM Mark Phillips said the government has nothing to hide and pledged legal consequences for anyone found responsible, including for negligence or criminal wrongdoing.
Police detained the rescued captain and at least one other crew member; both reportedly tested positive for marijuana.

summary: A farewell letter from a long-standing Stabroek News correspondent on the paper's decision to close after almost four decades. title: 'One Guyana' put to the test as Parliament yet to meet on MV Barima tragedy
summary: Janette Bulkan builds a comparative argument from the 2018 murder of 17 fishermen (16 Guyanese) in Surinamese waters. She details how Surinamese civil society marched, farmers organised a collection for victims' families, and Suriname's Parliament unanimously passed a comprehensive motion on 10 May 2018 — with Guyana's National Assembly unanimously passing a similar opposition motion a day later. Against that precedent she charges that the MV Barima disaster has occasioned divisive rather than unifying action, citing a new organisation that announced itself by attacking the Leader of the Opposition. Her conclusion is that the leader promoting 'One Guyana' has yet to demonstrate leadership concretely.
argument: Suriname's unifying parliamentary and civic response to the 2018 murder of 17 fishermen shows what Guyana's leaders should be doing after MV Barima, and by that yardstick the government's 'One Guyana' slogan is unproven.
key_facts: Quotes the Kaieteur News editorial of 21 July on 'monuments to the hypocrisies that torment Guyanese'
On 27 April and 5 May 2018, 17 fishermen (16 Guyanese) were murdered at sea in Suriname's waters; 12 bodies never recovered, 11 of them Guyanese
Suriname's Parliament unanimously passed a comprehensive motion on 10 May 2018; Guyana's National Assembly passed a similar opposition motion a day later
Locates the disaster off the mouth of the Pomeroon River and says over 100 Guyanese died

Claims Parliament was yet to be convened and no days of national mourning had been announced - other outlets report three days of mourning were declared on 21 July, so the letter appears to predate or be unaware of that declaration
